claims.claim: **Definition:** for age and sex, the current weight or the rate of gain is well below what is expected, **or weight has dropped 2 or more major percentile lines.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Slow weight gain' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Slow_weight_gain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Nutrition is the main driver of growth under 2 years; most cases are inadequate caloric intake.** Causes are commonly multifactorial, with psychosocial stressors often significant, and there is not always a pathological cause.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Slow weight gain' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Slow_weight_gain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Length and head circumference are often preserved initially**, but may be affected if undernutrition is severe or prolonged.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Slow weight gain' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Slow_weight_gain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Expected average weight gain (a guide, not the minimum acceptable):** 0–3 months 150–200 g/week; 3–6 months 100–150 g/week; 6–12 months 70–90 g/week.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Slow weight gain' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Slow_weight_gain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Under 2 years: WHO growth standards**, correcting for prematurity (under 37 weeks) until 2 years. **2 years and over: CDC charts.** Use syndrome-specific charts (e.g. Down, Turner) where appropriate.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Slow weight gain' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Slow_weight_gain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A healthy, gaining baby may cross down to and track along a lower centile** than their birth weight in the first few months.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Slow weight gain' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Slow_weight_gain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Weight under the 3rd percentile in isolation**, with typical neurodevelopment and no red flags, may still be normal — **monitor over time**; extensive investigation may not be needed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Slow weight gain' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Slow_weight_gain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A percentile drop on switching from WHO to CDC charts** is usually a chart artefact, not a true change in growth.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Slow weight gain' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Slow_weight_gain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Intake history:** breast or bottle, how many feeds per 24 hours and their volume/duration, breast milk supply, **formula preparation**; milk intake per 24 hours in toddlers.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Slow weight gain' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Slow_weight_gain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Examine** muscle bulk (buttocks), fat stores (thighs), and the eyes, gums, nails, hair and skin; development, caregiver–child interaction and **signs of abuse or neglect**; **observe a feed if able.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Slow weight gain' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Slow_weight_gain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **An otherwise healthy, normally developing child with no suggestive features needs no investigations at first.** Otherwise investigate according to the features elicited.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Slow weight gain' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Slow_weight_gain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Urine microscopy and culture — especially under 12 months, where slow weight gain may be the only sign of an occult UTI.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Slow weight gain' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Slow_weight_gain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Bloods to consider:** FBE, ferritin, UEC, TSH, glucose, LFT; **coeliac serology and total IgA** if eating gluten; micronutrients, especially active B12 if malabsorption or restricted diet is suspected.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Slow weight gain' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Slow_weight_gain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Stool:** microscopy, fat globules, fatty acid crystals. **Over 12 months:** add ESR and faecal calprotectin.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Slow weight gain' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Slow_weight_gain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Inadequate intake or retention:** inadequate nutrition, breastfeeding difficulties, **formula preparation error**, restricted diets (including vegan, sensory aversions), cleft palate, persistent vomiting, appetite loss from chronic disease, **solids introduced early (before 4 months) or late (after 6 months).**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Slow weight gain' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Slow_weight_gain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Psychosocial:** parental mental or chronic illness, poor carer understanding, non-secure attachment, mealtime difficulties, **coercive feeding (including feeding while asleep)**, food insecurity, isolation, missed appointments, substance abuse, **family violence, trauma or neglect**, child protection involvement.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Slow weight gain' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Slow_weight_gain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Poor absorption:** cow milk protein allergy, coeliac disease, pancreatic insufficiency (e.g. CF), chronic diarrhoea, chronic liver disease. **Excess utilisation:** UTI, chronic inflammation, chronic respiratory disease, congenital heart disease, diabetes, hyperthyroidism.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Slow weight gain' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Slow_weight_gain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Use a multidisciplinary team.** Management is guided by the contributing factors; **most children are managed as outpatients — consider admission if red flags are present.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Slow weight gain' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Slow_weight_gain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consult the paediatric team** for significant dehydration, illness or malnutrition; outpatient management that has failed; **concern about abuse or neglect**; significant parental mental health concern.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Slow weight gain' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Slow_weight_gain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider transfer** for severe malnutrition, or an underlying cause needing specialist input.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Slow weight gain' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Slow_weight_gain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge with a clear individualised plan:** feeding plan, and follow-up including outstanding investigations.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Slow weight gain' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Slow_weight_gain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Weigh infants every 1–4 weeks**, depending on concern. **One clinician (often the child health nurse or GP) owns follow-up** and ensures appointments are attended.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Slow weight gain' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Slow_weight_gain/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Missed follow-up: act to check the child's wellbeing; refer to Child Protection if at risk.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Slow weight gain' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Slow_weight_gain/, retrieved 2026-09-23
